beats.narration_en: This car just drifted into a concrete wall, yet its body never touched it. Only the tire did.
Against a flat wall, the same shallow hit lands on the body itself: first the front corner, then the rear.
A Jersey barrier is shaped differently. Its lower face leans back like a short, steep ramp.
The tire meets that slope first and climbs it, squeezing the suspension, which soaks up the hit.
Riding along the slope, the tire steers the car back toward its lane, with the body barely scratched.
That is why this simple concrete shape lines highways and work zones all across America.
